title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-avery-kim-2
content:
Quick PR review scratchpad for PR #3421 (KV cache + batching refactor)

High-level:
- Goal: simplify KV cache ownership model, reduce lock contention during batching, and add a single-codepath for eviction to avoid double-free issues.
- Scope: runtime/kv_cache/*, batching/worker_pool changes, some RPC surface tweaks (internal-only).
- Risks: subtle race around cache insert+evict during concurrent reads; perf regressions for short sequences if batching heuristics change.

Notes / questions to author:
- Why was LRUMap chosen over shard-based segmented map? comment mentions lower memory overhead but not contention profile. Any perf numbers?
- The cache eviction callback runs on the main goroutine (line ~512) — can this block request threads? consider offloading to worker pool.
- The new atomic refcount in kv_entry: do we need a finalizer or explicit free? I saw a couple places where .release() is called conditionally — path coverage looks incomplete.
- test_coverage: missing a high-concurrency test simulating interleaved insert/evict/read (see tests/kv_cache/concurrency_test.go). Add scenario with bursts and slow eviction.

Checklist for merge (my recommendations):
- [ ] Add microbench: cache insert/read under 8/32/128 concurrent clients (benchmark scripts in infra/bench). Collect p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput.
- [ ] Add deterministic unit test for double-free: create entry, spawn reader that holds ref across eviction TTL, assert no use-after-free.
- [ ] Move eviction callback to background thread or worker pool and measure effect on tail latency.
- [ ] Document invariants in code comments: ownership, who can call release(), and when entry->data may be nil.
- [ ] Add feature flag for opt-in rollout (kv-cache-refactor-2024Q4). Plan canary on staging then prod-dedicated.
- [ ] Add CI lint/fmt step: noticed mixed tabs/spaces in runtime/kv_cache/entry.go (run gofmt).

Refactor ideas (follow-ups, not blockers):
- Evaluate shard-per-core cache with per-shard locks; might eliminate global CP contention for read-heavy workloads.
- Introduce a small per-request transient cache to coalesce repeated reads within same request (prefix cache). Could be optional to avoid perf cliff for short seqs.
- Consider memory-accounting abstraction to keep per-tenant memory bounded in Dedicated mode (tie to tenant quotas).

Perf notes from quick local run (devbox, A100-sim):
- Baseline (main before PR): read-only throughput ~120k req/s, p95 latency 6.2ms
- With PR (single-shard, no eviction offload): throughput 108k req/s, p95 7.8ms (regression ~10-12%)
- After moving eviction offload to worker pool (experimental): throughput 118k req/s, p95 6.5ms — closer to baseline. Need proper bench.

Testing matrix to add to CI:
- unit: deterministic eviction/no-double-free (go test -run TestKVDoubleFree)
- stress: 5min stress tests at 500 concurrent clients in CI staging (flake tolerant)
- perf: nightly benchmark comparing baseline vs refactor across seq lengths {16,64,512}

Rollout plan (high-level):
1) merge behind feature flag 
2) canary on staging + internal traffic (2 days)
3) canary on prod-dedicated for low-traffic customers (48h)
4) enable on all dedicated clusters (monitor p95/p99 + error rates)

Follow-ups (after merge):
- create a GH issue to evaluate sharded cache (assign to Samir)
- add telemetry counters for eviction rate, contention_count, average_refcount_lifetime
- update docs: runtime/ops/kv-cache.md with new configuration knobs and default heuristics

Misc small nits (non-blocking):
- rename variables: `evictQ` -> `evictionQueue` for clarity
- inline comment typo: s/contenstion/contention/
- remove debug println in kv_cache manager (leftover)

Slack refs / context: see thread #kv-cache-refactor in #eng-serving-runtime (esp messages from @samir). Confluence draft linked above has proto diagrams.

Next steps for me:
- ask author for perf numbers used to pick LRUMap
- run local bench with eviction offload and snapshot results
- add missing unit test example to tests/kv_cache/concurrency_test.go

Notes to self:
- prioritize safety tests over micro-optimizations. if uncertain, prefer offloading eviction to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- keep PR small: avoid coupling to tenant memory accounting in this PR (follow up).

---
History: started notes 2024-11-07 during initial review. updated with perf run 2024-11-10.
